s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of neurological and respiratory symptoms with multi-organ involvement and evidence of infection
salient_findings: Respiratory failure with lower lobe nodules and infiltrate
key_facts: Patient is around 60 years old
Patient lives in a rural area in the southeastern US
Patient has a history of porphyria with polyneuropathy
Patient has a history of alcohol use disorder
Patient has a recent diagnosis of hyper-IgE syndrome
Patient was taking oral prednisone before admission
Patient presented with fever and respiratory distress
Bronchoalveolar lavage revealed Aspergillus fumigatus, Candida spp, and Pseudomonas aeruginosa
Autopsy findings showed disseminated aspergillosis and candidiasis
Multiple organ involvement including lungs, liver, pancreas, colon, appendix, and kidneys

raw.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of neurological and respiratory symptoms with multi-organ involvement and evidence of infection
salient_findings: Respiratory failure with lower lobe nodules and infiltrate
key_facts: Patient is around 60 years old
Patient lives in a rural area in the southeastern US
Patient has a history of porphyria with polyneuropathy
Patient has a history of alcohol use disorder
Patient has a recent diagnosis of hyper-IgE syndrome
Patient was taking oral prednisone before admission
Patient presented with fever and respiratory distress
Bronchoalveolar lavage revealed Aspergillus fumigatus, Candida spp, and Pseudomonas aeruginosa
Autopsy findings showed disseminated aspergillosis and candidiasis
Multiple organ involvement including lungs, liver, pancreas, colon, appendix, and kidneys

differentials: Hyper IgE syndrome with fungal infection
per_call: Hyper IgE syndrome with fungal infection

shortlist.label: Disseminated aspergillosis
shortlist.why_kept: Autopsy findings showed disseminated aspergillosis and patient had recent diagnosis of hyper-IgE syndrome, increasing susceptibility to fungal infections

shortlist.label: Candidiasis
shortlist.why_kept: Autopsy findings showed disseminated candidiasis and patient had recent diagnosis of hyper-IgE syndrome, increasing susceptibility to fungal infections

shortlist.label: Dirofilariasis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presented with flaccid paralysis and respiratory distress, and pathological findings showed larval sections in the eye, consistent with dirofilariasis

shortlist.label: Toxocariasis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presented with altered mental status, fever, and flaccid paralysis, and lived in a rural area, increasing the likelihood of toxocariasis

shortlist.label: Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection
shortlist.why_kept: Bronchoalveolar lavage revealed Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and patient had recent diagnosis of hyper-IgE syndrome, increasing susceptibility to bacterial infections

raw.rationale: Autopsy findings of larval sections in the eye and a coiled, incompletely sectioned filariform larva within a medium-caliber artery are consistent with Dirofilariasis, a parasitic infection caused by Dirofilaria species, which is common in rural areas of the southeastern US and can cause ocular and systemic symptoms

rejected.label: Disseminated aspergillosis
rejected.why: While the patient had disseminated aspergillosis, the presence of larval sections in the eye is not consistent with this diagnosis

rejected.label: Candidiasis
rejected.why: Candidiasis does not typically cause the presence of larval sections in the eye

rejected.label: Toxocariasis
rejected.why: Toxocariasis typically causes visceral or ocular larva migrans, but the presence of a coiled, incompletely sectioned filariform larva is more consistent with Dirofilariasis

rejected.label: Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection
rejected.why: Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection does not explain the presence of larval sections in the eye
